transcript: Five Models In Ruins, 1981 is the rather cinematic title of the play opening tonight at Lincoln Center's Claire Tow Theater. Unfortunately, it doesn't live up to its title. Set in English countryside, Roberta is shooting a cover for Vogue and it's a straight-up disaster. The setup is a mess, the models are catty, and Roberta is emotionally in shambles. An entertaining premise, for sure, but I thought this was poorly executed. Some of the writing was funny and unhinged and the performances were fine, but I struggled with caring about the characters and the fact that nothing really happened. I think it's meant to be a slice of life and a character study, but the tone was too inconsistent for that — I couldn't discern whether these characters were meant to be taken earnestly or ironically, so it was hard to know what to invest in or generally what this piece was trying to say. The most interesting character didn't show up until about halfway through the 100 minutes, and doing so brought a well-needed jolt of energy which more or less carried the rest of the play. But all in all, I found this to be pretty unfocused and confusing. For anyone who has seen and enjoyed the play, as there were definitely folks in the audience who seemed to enjoy it more than I did, I'd be curious to hear any opinions on who the target audience is and what the takeaways are meant to be. With that, another program for my collection.
